title: Who I am
cando: give personal details, spell names, and fill in a simple form

about.text: In this lesson you meet a new neighbour. You say where you are from and spell your name. You ask questions with do and does. Then you read a library form and fill in your own.
goals: Say who you are and where you are from: I'm from Egypt.
Spell your name, one letter at a time: S-A-M-I-R.
Ask and answer with do and does: Do you work here? Yes, I do.
Read a library form and an appointment card.
Join a library: answer the questions and give your details.

chapters.title: A new neighbour
chapters.text:
In this lesson you meet a new neighbour.
Samir is new in Park Road. He meets Lena. She lives next door.
They say hello and ask two questions. Where are you from? Do you work near here?
Lena writes Samir's name in her phone. She asks: How do you spell it?
Samir says the letters, one at a time. S-A-M-I-R.

chapters.title: am, is, are, and do, does
chapters.text:
First, am, is and are.
I am. He is. She is. You are. We are. They are.
Often we say the short form: I'm from Egypt. She's a nurse.
Then, questions with do and does.
With I, you, we and they, say do. Do you work here? Yes, I do. No, I don't.
With he and she, say does. Does she work here? Yes, she does. No, she doesn't.
After does, the verb has no s. Where does he live?

chapters.title: A form and a card
chapters.text:
Next, you read a form for a library card.
A form asks for your details. Your first name, your surname, your address and your postcode.
Many forms say: write in capital letters. Capital letters are easy to read.
Then you read an appointment card. Look for the day, the time and what to bring.
Last, you write about yourself and fill in a form.

chapters.title: Joining the library
chapters.text:
Then you join a library.
The person at the desk asks questions. What's your first name? And your surname?
Spell your name slowly and clearly. Y-U-S-U-F.
Say your date of birth, your address and your postcode.
When the question starts with do, give a short answer. Yes, I do. No, I don't.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about a person in a new town.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You meet a new neighbour. What do you say first?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people say hello and their name first. Welcome is a kind word for someone new.

conversation.title: A new neighbour
conversation.setting: Samir is new in Park Road. He meets Lena outside. She lives next door.
lines: Hello! Are you the new neighbour?
Yes, I am. I'm Samir. I live next door, at number 14.
Welcome! Nice to meet you. I'm Lena, from number 12.
Nice to meet you too. Where are you from, Lena?
I'm from Poland, from a small town. And you?
I'm from Egypt. I'm from a big city, Alexandria.
No, I don't. It's all new to me.
Yes, I do. I'm a nurse at the hospital. And you?
I work at the library. My husband doesn't work. He's a student.
I'm married too. My wife starts work next week.
Can I put your name in my phone? How do you spell it?
S-A-M-I-R. And my surname is Haddad: H-A-D-D-A-D.

questions.why: Samir says: I'm a nurse at the hospital.
Lena says: My husband doesn't work. He's a student.

phrases.use: Asking a person who is new in your street.
Asking about someone's country or town.
Asking for the letters of a name or a word.

items.meaning: A person who lives next to you or near you.
items.example: My neighbour works at the hospital.

items.meaning: In the house or flat right beside yours.
items.example: Samir lives next door, at number 14.

items.meaning: Not old. Also: here for the first time.
items.example: I'm new in this town.

items.meaning: People are happy that you are here.
items.example: You are always welcome in our home.

items.meaning: To have something in your head: a fact, a name, a place. You can also do this with a person.
items.example: Do you know my neighbour, Lena?

items.meaning: To say a question to a person.
items.example: Can I ask you a question?

items.meaning: To say or write something back when a person asks you.
items.example: Please answer the questions on the form.

items.meaning: A big land with its own name and flag, like Egypt or Poland.
items.example: Which country are you from?

items.meaning: A very big town, with many streets, shops and people.
items.example: I'm from a big city in the north.

items.meaning: A place with houses, shops and streets. It is smaller than a city.
items.example: Lena is from a small town.

items.meaning: A very small place with only a few houses and streets.
items.example: My parents live in a village.

items.meaning: With a husband or a wife.
items.example: I'm married. My wife is a teacher.

sound.title: I'm, don't, doesn't
sound.explain: Two words often become one short word. I am is I'm. Do not is don't. Does not is doesn't. Say each short form fast, as one word. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Samir's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Are I'm and don't each one short word?
lines: Yes, I am. I'm Samir. I live next door, at number 14.
I'm from Egypt. I'm from a big city, Alexandria.
No, I don't. It's all new to me.
S-A-M-I-R. And my surname is Haddad: H-A-D-D-A-D.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Two use be: am, is or are. Two use do or does.
examples: Do you work near here? Yes, I do.
spot.question: What is I'm in two words? Which word starts the question about work? Why does Lena say doesn't, not don't?
spot.answer: I'm = I am. Are goes with you: Where are you from? The question about work starts with do: Do you work near here? Yes, I do. My husband is he, and he goes with does: he doesn't work.

rules.title: am, is, are
rule: I am (I'm) · he, she, it is (he's, she's) · you, we, they are
I'm a nurse. She's from Poland. They're my neighbours.
Question: Are you new here? Where is he from?
No: I'm not married. He isn't at home.
rules.mistake: Not: I from Egypt. Say: I am from Egypt, or I'm from Egypt.

rules.title: Questions with do and does
rule: I, you, we, they: Do you work here? Yes, I do. No, I don't.
He, she, it: Does she work here? Yes, she does. No, she doesn't.
After does, the verb has no s: Where does he live?
A question word goes first: Where do you live? What does she do?
rules.mistake: Not: Does he works here? Say: Does he work here?

practice.q: Lena and her husband ___ from Poland.
practice.why: Lena and her husband are they, so are.
A question with you and a verb starts with do.
Your wife is she, so does.

practice.q: Does he speak English? Yes, he ___ .
practice.why: The question has does, so the answer has does.

practice.q: Do you know the town? No, I ___ .

practice.why: After does, the verb has no s.

practice.q: My husband ___ work. He's a student.
___ your neighbour married? Yes, she is.
practice.why: The answer has is, so the question starts with is.
The letters of a word answer How do you spell it?

yourTurn.prompt: A new neighbour asks about you. Write four or five sentences. Say your name, where you are from, where you live and your job. Use don't or doesn't one time.
yourTurn.model: My name is Priya. I'm from India, from a big city. I live next door, at number 16. I'm a cook in a café. I'm married, but my husband doesn't live here yet.

text.title: A library form and an appointment card
text.body:
PRACTICE FORM: this library does not exist

NORTHFIELD LIBRARY
NEW LIBRARY CARD
Please write in capital letters.

First name: AMINA
Surname: YUSUF
Date of birth: 14/03/1990
Nationality: SOMALI
Address: FLAT 3, 22 HILL ROAD, NORTHFIELD
Postcode: NF4 7QT
Email: amina.yusuf@mailbox.example
Phone: 07700 900 123

The card is free.

---

NORTHFIELD LIBRARY JOB CLUB
APPOINTMENT CARD

Name: Amina Yusuf
With: Ms Okafor, job adviser
Day: Tuesday 9 April
Time: 10.30
Where: Room 2, first floor

Please bring your library card.
Can't come? Please phone us the day before.

gist.a: a form for a library card, and a card with a time to come
wrong: a job advert and a timetable
gist.why: The form asks for Amina's details, and the appointment card gives a day and a time.
Amina's name is on the form and on the card.

detail.why: Surname: YUSUF. Amina is her first name.
Postcode: NF4 7QT. 22 Hill Road is her address, and 07700 900 123 is her phone.

detail.q: What must Amina bring to the appointment?
detail.why: The card says: Please bring your library card.

items.meaning: A paper or a web page with questions. You write your details in the boxes.
items.example: Please fill in this form.

items.meaning: Your own name, not your family name.
items.example: My first name is Amina.

items.meaning: Your family name.
items.example: Please write your surname in capital letters.

items.meaning: The number, street and town of your home.
items.example: My address is 22 Hill Road, Northfield.

items.meaning: Letters and numbers at the end of an address. They help the post find your home.
items.example: What's your postcode?

items.meaning: The day, month and year you were born.
items.example: My date of birth is 14 March 1990.

items.meaning: The country on your passport. For example: Somali, Polish, British.
items.example: What's your nationality? I'm Polish.

items.meaning: A message on a computer or a phone. Also the address for these messages.
items.example: What's your email address?

items.meaning: A building with books. You can take them home and bring them back later.
items.example: The library opens at nine o'clock.

items.meaning: A small, flat piece of hard paper or plastic. It often has your name on it.
items.example: Here is your new library card.

write.task: Write three sentences about yourself, like the model. Then fill in a form: first name, surname, nationality, address, postcode and email. You can use made-up details.
checklist: I wrote my first name and my surname.
I used I'm or I am in two sentences.
I filled in six lines of the form.
The form is in capital letters.

card.title: Join the library
card.situation: You want a card for Northfield Library. You are at the front desk. The assistant asks you questions and fills in the form.
card.goal: Answer the questions. Spell your surname, and give your date of birth, address and postcode.

phrases: Hello. I'd like to join the library, please.
My first name is Amina. My surname is Yusuf.
My date of birth is 14 March 1990.
My address is 22 Hill Road, and the postcode is NF4 7QT.
Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
prepare.notes: Write your details first: first name, surname, date of birth, nationality, address, postcode and email. Then practise the letters of your surname and your street.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is at the library desk. Answer the questions and spell your name. Then change roles: you ask, and your teacher answers.
doIt.wehel: You work at the front desk of a library. I want a library card. Ask me my first name, surname, date of birth, nationality, address, postcode and email. Ask me to spell my surname. Use simple English.

model.title: At the library desk
lines: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes, please. I'd like to join the library.
Of course. What's your first name?
Amina. And my surname is Yusuf.
How do you spell your surname?
Thank you. What's your date of birth?
Flat 3, 22 Hill Road. The postcode is NF4 7QT.
Do you have an email address?
compare: Did you say: I'd like to join the library?
Did you spell your surname clearly, one letter at a time?
Did you give your date of birth, address and postcode?
Did you answer the do question with a short answer: Yes, I do?

canDo: I can say where I am from and what I do.
I can spell my name and my street.
I can ask and answer questions with do and does.
I can read a form and an appointment card.
I can fill in a form with my details.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Who is the person? Where are they from, do you think?
reading.talk: What do you know about the person in the story now? Write three sentences about them, or tell Wehel about yourself.

quiz.q: ___ your husband work? Yes, he does.
quiz.why: Your husband is he, so does.

quiz.q: Do they know the town? No, they ___ .
A very small place with only a few houses is a ___ .
quiz.why: A village is smaller than a town.

quiz.q: On a form, NF4 7QT is your ___ .
quiz.why: A postcode has letters and numbers at the end of an address.

quiz.q: A new neighbour says: Hello, I'm Samir. I live next door. What do you say?
quiz.why: We say welcome to a person who is new.

quiz.q: My head ___ . Can you help me?
quiz.why: My head is one part, so hurts, with s.
Excuse me comes before a question to a stranger.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the neighbour conversation in pairs, then change the names, the countries and the jobs.
Day 2: find someone who. Learners ask each other do and does questions: Do you live in a city? Does your family live here?
Day 3: the library desk. You are the assistant. Each learner joins the library and spells their surname; then change roles.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and let two learners read their About me writing aloud.
